text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty alert PD-7821 fired for vf-inference-prod - HIGH. Escalation policy 'prod-inference' started. Primary oncall @olivia was paged. Link: https://pd.example.com/incidents/PD-7821 | Runbook: https://wiki/internal/runbooks/vf-inference

pagerduty-bot: PD-7821: Primary did not acknowledge within 2m. Escalating to secondary @sam. Escalation chain: primary -> secondary -> manager. Trigger: 5xx spike from 0.4% -> 6.2% over 3m.

olivia: ugh, just woke up — my phone was on DND, didn't get the page. trying to ack now. sorry all. :sleepy:

pagerduty-bot: PD-7821: Acknowledge attempt by olivia received but not registered due to retry failure. Secondary notified.

sam: acked. jumping in. creating bridge and grabbing logs. bridge: https://meet.example.com/room/incident-7821.

sam: quick context: customers reporting higher latency + 502s. first seen around 22:11 UTC. rolling window shows tail latency increase.

jas: looking at serving logs on vm-inf-03: seeing repeated: `kv_cache miss -> backend fetch timeout` and occasional `gpu OOM` during tokenization stage. snippet:
```
[22:12:03] ERROR inference_runner.cpp:542 - KVCache::Get failed: timeout after 5000ms
[22:12:04] WARN  model_executor.cpp:103 - GPU0 OOM while allocating 1.2GB
[22:12:05] ERROR http_server.cpp:221 - send_response() 502 upstream read timeout
```

sam: can we scale the pool? starting a hot-add of 4 replicas in us-west-2 now. `infractl pool scale vf-prod-inference --add 4`

pagerduty-bot: PD-7821: Secondary @sam acknowledged at +3m. Manager escalation to @maria will fire at +10m if no resolution.

maria: I'm on call-manage rotation, jumping in as manager. tagging ops-manager for awareness. Maria here — what's current customer impact? need quick numbers to message CS.

jas: current metrics (last 5m): total requests 48k, 5xx count 3.1k (6.4%), median latency 1.2s -> 8.6s, p95 18.3s. Two enterprise tenants showing >10% error rate.

sam: scaled replicas done, also temporarily routed heavy tails to fallback model `small-ml-v2` to reduce mem pressure: `trafficctl route add --service vf-inference --model small-ml-v2 --weight 10%`

olivia: FYI I managed to ack via Slack DM to pagerduty (phone still flaky). happy to help with logs if needed but will hand primary to sam for this one.

ops-manager: pinged CSMs for the two affected tenants, preparing a short status update. keep me posted if customer impact increases.

jas: after scaling + fallback route: 5xx dropped to 0.9% within ~6m. latency improved to median 1.8s, p95 5.2s. still watching.

sam: found a correlated recent rollout job: `runtime-1.3.8` kernel selection change landed 22:05 and affected nvlink memory allocation on a subset of nodes. rolling back the runtime on the affected ASG now: `deployctl rollback runtime vf-inference --to 1.3.7 --filter asg=inf-asg-usw2-3`

jas: rollback applied to 6 nodes, health checks passing. logs no longer showing the OOM traces on those hosts.

maria: good work. ops-manager please update customers: brief note that we've mitigated the issue by scaling and rolling back a recent runtime change; monitoring for a full return to normal.

ops-manager: drafting message for CSMs / support: "Brief outage impacting inference latency and errors between 22:11-22:24 UTC. Mitigation applied; error rate now within normal bounds. Root cause under investigation." will send in 5.

sam: joining post-incident bridge to start RCA after stabilization. plan: collect kernel/runtime diffs, allocation traces, and a set of failing request IDs for eval.

jas: marking PD-7821 as manually resolved in PagerDuty. PD-7821: Resolved by sam at +18m.

incident-bot: PD-7821 marked RESOLVED. Summary: runtime kernel change caused memory allocation regressions on subset of nodes -> OOMs -> upstream timeouts. Mitigation: scaled replicas, routed 10% traffic to fallback model, rolled back runtime to 1.3.7. Follow-up: postmortem + action item to add preflight canary for runtime kernel changes.

maria: assigning postmortem owner to jas and sam. will schedule a 30m sync tomorrow to review. thanks everyone. :white_check_mark:
